meta.title: SSC Stenographer Grade C & D - Hard Elementary PYQ Practice Set
instructions: 100 questions are to be attempted in 30 minutes.
Questions are based on SSC Stenographer previous-year questions and topic-wise PYQ sets, with wording paraphrased for practice.
The paper focuses on elementary SSC topics but uses comparatively difficult PYQ patterns.
0.25 marks will be deducted for every incorrect answer.
Section timing: Reasoning - 7 minutes 30 seconds, General Awareness - 7 minutes 30 seconds, English - 15 minutes.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning - Hard Elementary Topics

questions.text: Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a row facing north. E has exactly two persons to his left. G sits immediately next to E. B is immediately right of F. Exactly three persons sit between G and F. A is immediately left of D. Who is at the extreme left?
questions.explanation: Placing E in the third position and applying the G-F/B constraints fixes F at the extreme left.

questions.text: Arrange these words in dictionary order: Fontina, Fondue, Fondled, Fondant, Fontanel, Fonder.
options: A) Fonder, Fondant, Fondled, Fondue, Fontanel, Fontina
B) Fondant, Fonder, Fondled, Fondue, Fontanel, Fontina
C) Fonder, Fondled, Fondant, Fondue, Fontina, Fontanel
D) Fondant, Fonder, Fondled, Fontanel, Fontina, Fondue
questions.explanation: Compare the letters from left to right and place all 'Fond...' words before 'Font...'; among Fond words the alphabetical order gives the stated sequence.

questions.text: In a code, ACTION becomes DFWFLK and BISHOP becomes ELVELM. How will MATTER be coded using the same rule?
questions.explanation: The coding transformation applied character-by-character to ACTION and BISHOP gives QDWQCO for MATTER.

questions.text: Find the next term: NLJ, JHF, FDB, BZX, ?
questions.explanation: Every corresponding letter moves backwards by a fixed changing interval, giving XVT.

questions.text: If 1 January 2017 was Sunday, what day was 1 January 2016?
questions.explanation: 2016 was a leap year, but only one day separates 1 January 2016 and 1 January 2017 after accounting for the leap-year calendar, giving Saturday.

questions.text: 216 : 3 :: ? : 4 :: 1728 : 6. Find the missing number.
questions.explanation: 216 = 6^3 and 3 is half of 6; 1728 = 12^3 and 6 is half of 12. Therefore 4 corresponds to 8^3 = 512.

questions.text: 35 is related to 1125 and 45 is related to 1925 according to one rule. Using the same rule, 85 is related to:
13 : 676 :: 6 : 144. Which number has the same relation with 9?
PLAY is coded as 54 and HAPPY as 66. Using the same method, how is SMILE coded?
questions.explanation: Add alphabet positions: S(19)+M(13)+I(9)+L(12)+E(5)=58.

questions.text: A is the sister of Y. Z is the father of A, while Y is the son of B. How is Z related to Y?
questions.explanation: Z is directly stated to be the father of A and A is Y's sister, so Z is also Y's father.

questions.text: All keys are locks. All locks are handles. Which conclusion follows? I. All keys are handles. II. Some handles are keys.
questions.explanation: Keys are a subset of locks and locks are a subset of handles, so all keys are handles. Existence of keys is not guaranteed, so II does not necessarily follow.

questions.text: Some chairs are holders. Some holders are bottles. Some bottles are chairs. Which statement is definitely true?
options: D) No bottle is a chair
questions.explanation: The third statement directly establishes that some bottles are chairs.

questions.text: No file is a folder. Some files are PDFs. All files are Excel sheets. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
options: A) Some Excel sheets are PDFs
C) No PDF is an Excel sheet
questions.explanation: Some files are PDFs and every file is an Excel sheet, therefore some Excel sheets are PDFs.

questions.text: Find the missing term: 17, 19, 22, 24, 27, ?
questions.explanation: The differences alternate +2, +3, +2, +3, so the next increase is +2, giving 29.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make 13 + 26 × 2 − 5 ÷ 4 = 6 correct?
questions.explanation: Interchanging + and ÷ and applying normal precedence makes the equation true.

questions.text: If + means ÷, − means +, × means − and ÷ means ×, which operation should replace the question mark in the resulting expression?
questions.explanation: Substitution must be performed exactly according to the coded-operation definitions before applying BODMAS.

questions.text: A person walks 6 km north, turns right and walks 4 km, then turns right and walks 6 km. In which direction is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: The north and south movements cancel, leaving a displacement of 4 km east.

questions.text: In a row of students, Rahul is 17th from the left and 21st from the right. How many students are there in total?
Find the next term: 5, 14, 41, 122, 365, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is multiplied by 3 and then 1 is subtracted: 365 × 3 − 1 = 1094.

questions.text: Find the missing number: 11 : 256 :: 14 : 361 :: ? : 1024.
In an arrangement, M is next to L, J is second to the left of L and N is not at an end. O is next to N. If O is diagonally opposite J, which type of arrangement is being described?
questions.explanation: The use of 'diagonally opposite' indicates two parallel rows rather than a single straight row.

questions.text: Three of the following number pairs follow the same relation. Which is the odd one?
questions.explanation: The relation in the original analogous PYQ is based on a slightly different transformation; 12:144 breaks the intended comparison set.

questions.text: Find the next term: 122, 135, 161, 200, 252, ?
questions.explanation: The successive differences are 13, 26, 39, 52, so the next difference is 65; 252 + 65 = 317.

questions.text: Which word is related to 'Fanaticism' in the same way that 'Hatred' is related to 'Bigotry'?
questions.explanation: Fanaticism is closely associated with zealotry, just as bigotry is associated with hatred.

questions.text: If 38 ÷ 19 × 11 − 357 + 17 = 226, which pair of signs must be interchanged?
questions.explanation: The original SSC operation-interchange question is solved by testing the sign swaps under normal arithmetic precedence.

sections.name: General Awareness - Hard Static Elementary Topics

questions.text: Which Act of British India proposed the creation of an All-India Federation?
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act 1935 proposed an All-India Federation.

questions.text: Banabhatta, the court poet of Harshavardhana, is associated with which work?
questions.explanation: Harshacharita is Banabhatta's celebrated account of Harshavardhana.

questions.text: Who is regarded as an early pioneer of microbiology for observing microorganisms with microscopes?
questions.explanation: Leeuwenhoek's microscopic observations of microorganisms earned him his foundational place in microbiology.

questions.text: The Nehru Trophy Boat Race is associated with which state?
questions.explanation: The Nehru Trophy Vallam Kali is held in Kerala.

questions.text: Tanjore Balasaraswati was a famous exponent of which classical dance?
questions.explanation: Tanjore Balasaraswati was one of the major Bharatanatyam performers.

questions.text: Which of the following is a non-metal and therefore a poor conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Sulphur is a non-metal and does not conduct electricity well.

questions.text: Which organelle contains ribosomal RNA together with proteins?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are ribonucleoprotein particles composed of rRNA and proteins.

questions.text: What process converts decomposed organic matter into humus?
questions.explanation: Humification is the process responsible for humus formation.

questions.text: Which gas is primarily filled into packets of potato chips to prevent oxidation?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen provides an inert atmosphere and reduces oxidation of the chips.

questions.text: What is the reverse process of deposition?
questions.explanation: Deposition changes gas directly into solid; sublimation is the reverse, solid directly into gas.

questions.text: Which gas is popularly known as marsh gas?
questions.explanation: Methane is commonly called marsh gas.

questions.text: The process in which water vapour turns back into liquid water is called:
questions.explanation: Condensation converts a gas or vapour into a liquid.

questions.text: Which state is NOT a major rubber-producing state among the following?
questions.explanation: Punjab is not a major natural-rubber producing state.

questions.text: Who wrote the autobiography 'My Country My Life'?
questions.explanation: The autobiography is by L.K. Advani.

questions.text: Which of the following is a statutory rather than a constitutional body?
questions.explanation: RBI was established by the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, making it statutory.

questions.text: Which is the oldest mountain range among those listed?
questions.explanation: The Aravalli range is among the oldest fold mountain systems in the world.

questions.text: The Amaravati school of sculpture is especially known for extensive use of:
questions.explanation: Amaravati is particularly known for detailed limestone bas-reliefs.

questions.text: Which festival marks the birth anniversary of Lord Jhulelal?
questions.explanation: Cheti Chand is the major Sindhi festival associated with Jhulelal.

questions.text: Which Rashtrakuta ruler is associated with defeating the Cholas?
questions.explanation: Krishna III achieved major victories against the Cholas.

questions.text: Which musician is especially associated with Carnatic vocal music?
questions.explanation: M. Balamuralikrishna was a major Carnatic vocalist and composer.

questions.text: The Indian Iron and Steel Company established its first factory at which place?
questions.explanation: The Indian Iron and Steel Company established its first major factory at Burnpur.

questions.text: According to Census 2011, India's decadal population growth rate for 2001-2011 was approximately:
questions.explanation: India's population grew by about 17.64% during 2001-2011.

questions.text: Which rice variety was popularly described as a 'miracle rice' because of its exceptional yield in India?
questions.explanation: IR8 became famous as a high-yielding miracle rice variety associated with the Green Revolution.

questions.text: How far is the penalty spot from the goal line in football?
questions.explanation: The penalty mark is 11 metres from the goal line.

questions.text: Which institution became the source of the equation C = K Pgas in the context of gas-solubility studies?
questions.explanation: The relation corresponds to Henry's law, connecting dissolved gas concentration with gas pressure.

sections.name: English Language & Comprehension - Hard Elementary Topics

questions.text: Choose the correct replacement: 'Harsha is the tallest than all the other boys in his colony.'
questions.explanation: With the superlative 'tallest', the correct construction is 'the tallest of all the other boys'.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: A) It is easier to learn English than learn German.
B) It is easier learning English than to learn German.
C) It is easier to learn English than to learn German.
D) It is easier learn English than learning German.
questions.explanation: Parallel infinitive constructions are required: 'to learn English' and 'to learn German'.

questions.text: Choose the one-word substitute for 'an inclination or liking for history'.
questions.explanation: Predilection means a preference or special liking.

questions.text: Correct the sentence: 'The corner of the street where my family lived is surround by investigators.'
questions.explanation: The passive present construction requires 'is surrounded'.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: 'Unless he has permission from his parents, he ____ travel alone.'
questions.explanation: The first conditional uses present simple in the unless-clause and will not/won't in the main clause.

questions.text: Correct the question: 'When you will be award for your achievements?'
options: A) When will you be awarded for your achievements?
B) When will you awarded for your achievements?
C) When you will be awarded for your achievements?
D) When will you be award for your achievements?
questions.explanation: The correct passive interrogative is 'When will you be awarded...?'

questions.text: What is the closest meaning of 'incessant'?
questions.explanation: Incessant means continuing without interruption.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of 'reliable'.
questions.explanation: Untrustworthy is the direct opposite of reliable.

questions.text: Choose the synonym of 'vanquish'.
questions.explanation: Vanquish means defeat or conquer.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of 'admonish'.
questions.explanation: Admonish means to reprimand; applaud has the opposite positive sense.

questions.text: What does 'abscond' mean?
questions.explanation: To abscond means to leave secretly and hurriedly, often to avoid responsibility.

questions.text: What does the idiom 'get wind of' mean?
questions.explanation: To get wind of something means to receive information about it, often secretly.

questions.text: What does 'keep an eye on' mean?
questions.explanation: It means to watch or take care of someone or something.

questions.text: What does 'under the weather' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means to feel somewhat unwell.

questions.text: What does 'keep body and soul together' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means to manage to survive, often under difficult financial conditions.

questions.text: Change into indirect speech: He said, 'I have finished my homework.'
options: A) He said that he has finished his homework.
B) He said that he had finished his homework.
C) He said that he finished his homework tomorrow.
D) He said that he would finish his homework.
questions.explanation: Present perfect changes to past perfect after a past reporting verb.

questions.text: Change into indirect speech: She said to me, 'I shall come to meet you tomorrow.'
options: A) She told me that she would come to meet me the next day.
B) She said that she will come to meet me tomorrow.
C) She asked me whether she could come tomorrow.
D) She told me that she should come the next day.
questions.explanation: Shall changes to would, you changes according to the listener, and tomorrow becomes the next day.

questions.text: Change into indirect speech: 'Do you know the recipe?' my friend said to me.
options: A) My friend asked me whether I knew the recipe.
B) My friend asked me whether I know the recipe.
C) My friend told me whether I knew the recipe.
D) My friend asked that I knew the recipe.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question becomes 'asked whether/if' and the tense normally shifts back.

questions.text: Change into direct speech: She explained that she was playing the keyboard.
options: A) She explained, 'I was playing the keyboard.'
B) She explained, 'I am playing the keyboard.'
C) She explained, 'I have played the keyboard.'
D) She explained, 'I will play the keyboard.'
questions.explanation: Past continuous in reported speech corresponds to present continuous in direct speech.

questions.text: Change into direct speech: They said that they had been waiting for the bus for over an hour.
options: A) They said, 'We have been waiting for the bus for over an hour.'
B) They said, 'We had waited for the bus for over an hour.'
C) They said, 'We are waiting for the bus for over an hour.'
D) They said, 'We waited for the bus for over an hour.'
questions.explanation: Past perfect continuous in narration corresponds to present perfect continuous in the direct statement.

questions.text: Change into active voice: 'The cake was baked by the chef in the kitchen.'
options: A) The chef baked the cake in the kitchen.
B) The chef was baking the cake in the kitchen.
C) The chef has baked the cake in the kitchen.
D) The chef had baked the cake in the kitchen.
questions.explanation: The passive simple past becomes active simple past.

questions.text: Change into active voice: 'The wounded woman was being helped by some youngsters.'
options: A) Some youngsters helped the wounded woman.
B) Some youngsters were helping the wounded woman.
C) Some youngsters have helped the wounded woman.
D) Some youngsters had helped the wounded woman.
questions.explanation: Past continuous passive becomes past continuous active.

questions.text: Change into active voice: 'Parents should be respected by their children.'
options: A) Children should respect their parents.
B) Children should be respecting their parents.
D) Children will respect their parents.
questions.explanation: The modal 'should' remains unchanged and the passive object becomes the active subject.

questions.text: Change into passive voice: 'Who took Bruno for a walk?'
options: A) By whom was Bruno taken for a walk?
B) By whom Bruno was taken for a walk?
C) Who was Bruno taken for a walk?
D) By whom has Bruno been taken for a walk?
questions.explanation: Simple past active becomes simple past passive: 'By whom was Bruno taken...?'

questions.text: Change into passive voice: 'It is time to have tea.'
options: B) It is time for tea to be had.
C) Tea was had by it.
D) It has time to take tea.
questions.explanation: The accepted passive form uses 'for tea to be had'.

questions.text: Improve the sentence: 'He was the most cleverest man I ever knew.'
options: A) He was the cleverest man I ever knew.
B) He was the most cleverer man I ever knew.
C) He was a most cleverest man I ever knew.
D) He was more cleverest than I knew.
questions.explanation: Do not use both 'most' and '-est' together.

questions.text: Choose the correct articles: 'The Earth has ___ exceptional structure which may have helped in life's arrival.'
questions.explanation: 'Exceptional' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an exceptional structure' is correct.

questions.text: Choose the correct article pair: 'She took ___ unusual decision in ___ unprejudiced way.'
questions.explanation: Both 'unusual' and 'unprejudiced' begin with vowel sounds, requiring 'an'.

questions.text: Correct the sentence: 'He will has been helping me with tending to my plants.'
options: A) He will have been helping me with tending to my plants.
B) He will has helping me with tending to my plants.
C) He will be helped me with tending to my plants.
D) He has will been helping me with tending to my plants.
questions.explanation: After 'will', use the base auxiliary 'have': will have been helping.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: 'Elegance and intelligence ____ the two most important traits of young ladies.'
questions.explanation: The compound subject 'Elegance and intelligence' takes the plural verb 'are'.

questions.text: Choose the correct replacement: 'My idea can be key idea for solving difficult conflicts of extremely high level.'
questions.explanation: The singular countable noun 'idea' needs the article 'a' here.

questions.text: Choose the synonym of 'ignoramus'.
questions.explanation: An ignoramus is an ignorant or poorly informed person.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of 'constant'.
questions.explanation: Constant means unchanging or continuous; changing is its opposite.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of 'rapaciousness'.
questions.explanation: Rapaciousness means extreme greed; generosity is its opposite.

questions.text: Choose the synonym of 'assortment'.
questions.explanation: An assortment is a varied collection of things.

questions.text: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'hind'.
questions.explanation: Hind means situated at or toward the back.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: 'Technology allows us to deliver the same lessons in a much more ____ manner.'
questions.explanation: Resourceful gives the intended positive sense of effective use of available means.

questions.text: Select the correct sentence.
options: A) I have known her for many years.
B) I am knowing her for many years.
C) I had know her for many years.
D) I have been know her for many years.
questions.explanation: 'Know' is normally used in the simple present perfect for a state continuing up to the present.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: 'It is easier to learn English ____ to learn German.'
questions.explanation: Comparative constructions use 'than'.

questions.text: Identify the error: 'That accident happened a long time ago, but I have shivered at the thought of it ever for.'
options: B) happened a long time ago
C) I have shivered at the thought
questions.explanation: The final phrase is incorrectly ordered; 'ever since' would be required in a meaningful construction.

questions.text: Choose the correct form: 'Some students are known ____ wise early.'
questions.explanation: The construction is 'are known to grow'.

questions.text: Choose the correct word: 'The websites offer a huge ____ of products.'
questions.explanation: Assortment means a varied collection.

questions.text: Identify the correct phrase: 'The patient could not survive the injuries and ____.'
questions.explanation: The correct preposition after 'succumb' is 'to'.

questions.text: Choose the correct active form: 'Devotional songs are sung superbly by Sastri.'
options: A) Sastri sings devotional songs superbly.
B) Sastri sang devotional songs superbly.
C) Sastri is singing devotional songs superbly.
D) Sastri has sung devotional songs superbly.
questions.explanation: The passive is simple present, so the active is also simple present.

questions.text: Choose the correct replacement: 'I am not forced to study hard by my parents.'
options: A) My parents do not force me to study hard.
B) My parents did not force me to study hard.
C) My parents are not force me to study hard.
D) My parents will not forced me to study hard.
questions.explanation: The present passive is converted to present simple active.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of 'amplify'.
questions.explanation: Amplify means to increase or enlarge; lessen means to reduce.

questions.text: Choose the correctly arranged sentence: R = museums are always, S = treasure troves of information, P = showcasing historic objects, Q = by taking us back in time.
questions.explanation: The sentence logically begins with the subject 'museums are always', followed by its complement and descriptive clause.

questions.text: Choose the correct article: 'The Earth has ___ exceptional structure.'
questions.explanation: 'Exceptional' begins with the vowel sound /ɪ/, so 'an' is required.

questions.text: Choose the correct passive form of 'FIFA Cup 2022 will be won by France.'
options: A) France will win the FIFA Cup 2022.
B) France will be winning the FIFA Cup 2022.
C) France wins the FIFA Cup 2022.
D) France would win the FIFA Cup 2022.
questions.explanation: The given statement is passive; its active counterpart uses 'France will win'.

questions.text: Choose the correct active form of 'The cake was baked by the chef.'
options: A) The chef bakes the cake.
B) The chef baked the cake.
C) The chef has baked the cake.
D) The chef was baking the cake.
questions.explanation: Simple past passive changes to simple past active: 'The chef baked the cake.'
